body: Large language models (LLMs) often default to Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) when generating Arabic, even when prompted with dialectal Arabic. A natural explanation is that their internal representations are dominated by MSA. We test this hypothesis by adapting the language-dominance framework of Shani and Basirat (2025) (https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2025.blackboxnlp-1.7) to 26 Arabic varieties. Across layers and model families, we find no evidence that MSA acts as a dominant internal representation for Arabic dialects. Instead, dialect representations form a dense and highly overlapping space: normalized mutual information drops sharply compared to patterns reported for more distinct languages. Moreover, the strongest separability effects are not confined to intermediate layers, but can shift toward later layers depending on the architecture. These findings challenge a common interpretation of MSA-biased generation: output preference does not necessarily reveal internal representational dominance. Analyses of multilingual and dialectal LLMs should therefore distinguish generation bias from the geometry of internal representations.
summaryZh: 该研究调查了大型语言模型（LLMs）在生成阿拉伯语时是否以现代标准阿拉伯语（MSA）为主导。研究人员将语言主导框架应用于26种阿拉伯语变体，并分析了模型的内部表示。结果并未发现MSA在内部表示上主导阿拉伯方言的证据。相反，方言的表示形成了一个密集且高度重叠的空间，其分离效果会根据模型架构在不同层级变化。这挑战了“生成偏好反映内部表示主导地位”的常见解释，强调了在分析多语言和方言LLM时，区分生成偏差与内部表示几何结构的重要性。
